title: Existential target phase
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number, let $K$ be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $\sigma=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ be a nine-register state. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $t=0$, $tmp=0$, $p\le |x|$, and $n\le |x|$. Assume that for every $j<n$, whenever $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(j))$ holds, the program started at label $w0$ with target register $t=j$, input pointer $p=|x|$, and scratch register $tmp=0$ has property $K(j)$. Then the program started at label $tg$ in state $\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all registers at most $B$, and has an accepting branch exactly when there is some $j<n$ such that $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(j))$ and $K(j)$ both hold.
hypotheses_covered: $K$ is a predicate on natural numbers
Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For every $j<n$, if $\operatorname{PlainAt}(x,p,\operatorname{bits}(j))$, the indicated $w0$ computation has property $K(j)$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a finite bit string, let $B$ be a natural number with $2|x|+2\le B$, let $K$
be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $\sigma$ be a nine-register configuration
whose register values are all at most $B$. Suppose its target and scratch registers are
zero, its input pointer is at most $|x|$, and its vertex count is at most $|x|$. Assume
that for every $j<\sigma.n$, if the substring of $x$ beginning at position $\sigma.p$ is
exactly the canonical binary representation of $j$ and ends at the end of $x$, then the
program started at label $w0$ with target register $j$, input pointer $|x|$, and scratch
register zero has property $K(j)$. Then the program started at label $tg$ with
configuration $\sigma$ terminates on every branch with all register values bounded by
$B$, and has an accepting branch exactly when there is some $j<\sigma.n$ satisfying that
substring condition and $K(j)$.
